title: Afternoon trips at the dental office

dispatch.complaint: AC works in the morning, then every afternoon it starts blowing warm. Patients are complaining.

faults.description: Outdoor fan run capacitor failed (lost capacitance).
Compressor cycling off on HPC as head pressure climbs with no condenser airflow.

readings.txt_tstat: Thermostat: Cool, setpoint 72°F, space 77°F. Y1 and G on.
readings.txt_controller: No unit controller (electromechanical unit). No diagnostics. Compressor drops whenever HPC1 opens and restarts when it recloses.
readings.txt_look_unit: Compressor running, but the outdoor fan isn't turning. Motor hums. Compressor shuts off after a few minutes, then comes back on a few minutes later.
readings.txt_look_condenser: Outdoor fan stopped, motor humming and hot. Heat pouring off the coil. Coil itself is fairly clean.
readings.txt_look_electrical: CC1 pulled in. Capacitor CF top is slightly domed.

hints: A humming PSC motor that won't start: motor or capacitor?

diagnosis.label: Outdoor fan run capacitor failed
diagnosis.feedback: 0.8 µF on a 5 µF cap. The motor can't start, head goes through the roof, HPC opens.

diagnosis.label: Outdoor fan motor seized
diagnosis.feedback: Possible on a humming motor, but the cap measures dead. Test the cheap part first.

diagnosis.label: Faulty high-pressure switch
diagnosis.feedback: The HPC is doing its job. 560 psig liquid with no condenser airflow.

diagnosis.label: Overcharged
diagnosis.feedback: Subcooling is about 10°F. Charge looks fine. High head is from no airflow.

diagnosis.label: Dirty condenser coil
diagnosis.feedback: Coil's fairly clean, and the fan isn't even turning.

repair.label: Replace CF (match µF and VAC rating)
repair.feedback: Fan comes up to speed, head drops, unit stays on.

repair.label: Replace outdoor fan motor
repair.feedback: New motors usually ship with a cap, so it'll run, but you threw a $350 motor at a $25 problem.

repair.label: Reset HPC and restart
repair.feedback: It'll trip again in 10 minutes. Callback.

repair.label: Recover some charge
repair.feedback: Now you've undercharged it AND the fan's still dead.

idealPath.why: Fan not turning while the compressor runs. Big clue.
Voltage at the motor and humming amps: it's getting power but can't start.
Confirms high head from no airflow, and normal subcooling rules out overcharge.
Lock out before you touch the cap.
0.8 µF on a 5 µF cap. Dead.

debrief: Morning works, afternoon fails: heat-dependent. A weak cap can still start the fan when it's cool, then dies when it's hot. The HPC trip is the symptom; the cap is the root. Reset the HPC without finding the cap and you're back tomorrow.
